summary: The Fed's June meeting concluded with Chair Warsh holding rates steady at 3.50–3.75%, the vote unanimous at 12-0. The hawkish shift was the story: nine of 18 policymakers now project at least one rate hike by end-2026, driving bond yields higher, with the 2-year rising sharply to 4.21% as front-end rates bore the brunt of repricing.
tweet: Warsh's Fed flagged possible hikes — 9 of 18 officials projected at least one in 2026 — lifting front-end yields and pressuring risk assets across the board.
